name: Trap Bar Deadlift
notes: 2-3 sets x 2-3 reps @ RPE 6-7 only. No grinders. No soreness target.

name: Landmine Press → Med Ball Chest Pass
Single-Leg Balance (Eyes Closed)
notes: Progress by adding head turns or unstable surface

name: Tandem Gait Walk (Heel-to-Toe)
notes: Add backward walking for progression

name: Bosu Ball Mini-Squats
notes: Keep squats shallow (30° knee bend)

name: Foam Pad Alphabet Tracing
notes: Trace letters with toes while standing on one leg

name: Reactive Band Taps (Partner)
notes: Partner gently tugs band in random directions during single-leg stance

name: Single-Leg Medicine Ball Chest Push Jump
Atlas Stone Load Isometric (120% max stone @ lap)
KB Suitcase Carry
pro_tip: Hold KB opposite side of working leg to maximize oblique engagement - mimics sprawl recovery mechanics
combat_carryover: Develops clinch grip endurance and cross-body power transfer for hooks

name: Bird Dog Hold
notes: From quadruped, reach opposite arm and leg with trunk square. Stop on quality drop.

name: Isometric Mid-Thigh Pull
contraindications: skip when pins or trap bar are unavailable
avoid if maximal pulling intent irritates the low back
notes: Late-camp force-preservation pull from a fixed mid-thigh position. Keep total volume tiny and intent maximal.

name: Trap-Bar Pin Pull Isometric
contraindications: skip when pins or trap bar are unavailable
avoid if aggressive brace work spikes blood pressure during the cut
notes: 2–3x4–6s, full setup and full rest. Prioritise D-13; only use on D-7 if dose stays very low. Not for D-3 or D-1.

name: Punch-Specific Max Isometric Hold
contraindications: avoid if shoulder or wrist pain spikes when bracing against the bag
notes: D-7/D-3: 2-3 x 3-5s per side with full rest. D-1: 1-2 x 3-5s per side with clean submax to max intent only.

name: Overcoming Split-Squat Isometric
contraindications: skip if front-knee irritation increases with split-stance pressure
notes: 2-3 x 5-10s per leg with full rest. Use D-3 only as a tiny exposure when needed; avoid D-1 unless very light.

name: Staggered-Stance Medicine-Ball Punch Throw
contraindications: skip if trunk rotation is currently symptom-limited
notes: Low-volume punch throw from a fight stance. Keep it crisp, chest-height, and never chase fatigue.

name: Towel/Gi Row Isometric Hold
contraindications: skip if elbow tendons are already flared by heavy gripping
notes: Short-duration towel or gi row hold for grip and upper-back tension with almost no soreness cost.

name: Band-Resisted Jab-Cross Primer
contraindications: skip if shoulder speed drops or punching mechanics feel noisy
notes: Micro-dose band primer for crisp jab-cross sequencing. Keep reps low, fast, and fully recovered.

name: Adductor Squeeze Isometric
contraindications: skip if adductor squeeze increases groin pain beyond a mild awareness
notes: Gentle but high-value groin and pelvis tension touch that survives hard cuts and the final days before fighting.

name: Split-Stance Wall-Drive Isometric
notes: 2-3 x 5-8s per side with full reset. On D-1 keep to tiny clean exposures only.

name: Half-Kneeling Medicine-Ball Punch Throw
notes: 2-3 x 3 per side with full rest. Use D-3 only as micro-dose.

name: Seated Medicine-Ball Punch Throw
notes: 2-3 x 3 throws with full rest.

name: Landmine Split-Stance Punch Press
contraindications: avoid if shoulder symptoms are active
notes: 2-3 x 3 per side with full rest. Keep very light and avoid final-day use.

name: Technical Shadowboxing Tempo
notes: Short technical rhythm only; stop before fatigue or shoulder burn.

name: Light Heavy-Bag Technical Tempo
notes: Touch-speed bag rhythm only; no hard rounds or volume accumulation.

name: Mobility Reset Flow
notes: Easy mobility and breathing reset; keep it restorative, not a workout.
